name: Haus der Musik Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Haus der Musik Innsbruck on Rennweg: Tyrol's premier cultural center for concerts, theater, university music studies, and high-caliber acoustic arts.
beschreibung:
Overview

The architecturally striking Haus der Musik Innsbruck is situated on historic Rennweg in the heart of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck (Innsbruck region) at an altitude of approximately 574 meters. Opened in October 2018 on the site of the former traditional Stadtsaal, the building—designed by celebrated architect Erich Strolz—unites ten leading cultural and educational institutions under a single roof. With its dark, ceramic-shimmering louvered facade that subtly shifts tone depending on sunlight, this cultural venue forms a striking contemporary counterpart to the imperial Hofburg palace, the Tyrolean State Theatre, and the Hofgarten park.

Route & Requirements

The functional heart of the venue comprises several state-of-the-art auditoriums boasting extraordinary acoustic fidelity. The Great Hall (Großer Saal) accommodates up to 550 concertgoers and is equipped with advanced electroacoustic room simulation, creating flawless acoustic conditions for both symphonic orchestral performances and intimate chamber music. In the Small Hall (Kleiner Saal), seating around 100, and on two flexible studio stages (K2 and K3), audiences enjoy avant-garde theatrical productions, jazz sessions, literary readings, and youth workshops. Resident institutions include the Innsbruck Tyrolean Symphony Orchestra (TSOI), the Innsbruck Early Music Festival, the Tyrolean State Conservatory, the University of Innsbruck's Department of Musicology, and regional choral and wind band associations. Expansive, luminous foyers with floor-to-ceiling glass fronts command panoramic views of the soaring Nordkette mountain range.

Visit & Arrival

The Haus der Musik is open to performance attendees, concert guests, and restaurant patrons; the foyers generally open one hour before scheduled performances. Ticket prices vary depending on the promoter and program (concerts range from approx. €15.00 to €65.00, with many student and youth recitals offering free or heavily discounted admission). The in-house restaurant Das Brahms delights guests with refined regional and international culinary creations. Getting there: The venue is centrally located at Universitätsstraße 1 / Rennweg. From Innsbruck Central Station, it is an enjoyable ten-minute stroll through the pedestrian zone. Numerous city buses (including lines A, R, 501, 504) and trams 1 and 3 stop right nearby at Polizeidirektion or Landestheater. Motorists can use the Citygarage, Congressgarage, or Marktplatzgarage within easy walking distance.

Tips

All performance halls, visitor levels, dining spaces, and cloakrooms are fully barrier-free and accessible via spacious elevators; induction loops support hearing-impaired patrons. Before your trip to Innsbruck, check out the program of the world-renowned Innsbruck Early Music Festival in August, showcasing premier baroque opera productions and period ensembles in this acoustic jewel. A leisurely walk through the adjacent imperial Hofgarten before an evening concert is highly recommended.
oeffnungszeiten: Veranstaltungsabhängig; Foyers an Vorstellungstagen ab 1 h vor Beginn geöffnet
